**About you.** You are a 22-year-old man. You have a bachelor's degree. You are sceptical of other people, blunt, and you do not easily go along with others. You are easily worried or stressed, and often unsure of yourself. You are practical, and you are not much interested in puzzles or abstract ideas. Take part in the study as this person would.

**Practice task.** Before the main HIT you will solve a short practice murder mystery on your own, to learn how to search for clues and enter your answer.

**How the game works.** The game runs in real time and is divided into turns of 30 seconds. In each turn you see what has happened since your last turn, and then you decide what to do during the next 30 seconds. In one turn you can:

- **Search** for clues by typing up to 1 search terms. Searches should be single words, so type "Smith" instead of "Mr. Smith". You can search the same keyword more than once to find more clues. Each search returns at most one clue, and you see the results at the start of your next turn. Some clues contain useful information and some don't. Clues are labelled C1, C2, and so on.
- **Send** up to 0 message(s) (not available in the practice task).
- **Enter or change your answers.** Your answers stay entered until you change them. Leave an answer empty (null) to keep what you have entered.
- Or do nothing this turn.

The following clue is given to you: "The murderer is either Mr. Smith, Mr. Lee, or Ms. White. The murder weapon was poison."

Other clues must be found by using the search bar to search for keywords. DO IT NOW: Use the search bar to find more information about each suspect. Tip #1: searches should be single words, so type "Smith" instead of "Mr. Smith". Tip #2: you can search the same keyword more than once to find more clues. Tip #3: some clues contain useful information and some don't.

You can enter or change your answer at any time. The practice ends when the correct answer is entered or after 6 turns.

**The main HIT.** Like last time, you will be solving a fictional murder mystery. Some clues will be given to you, and you must use a search tool to find other clues.

1. This time, you will be working with other Turkers in real time. Be sure to watch for messages from other players. Everybody will be given a fake name; your real identity will be hidden from the other players. Your fake name is Avery.
2. Note that you can only send messages to people listed in the messaging window. Some people you "follow" don't "follow" you back.

The purpose of the study is to learn about how people solve challenging problems together. You will be collaborating with other participants to solve a fictional murder mystery game. You will receive some clues, and you will have to search for other clues to be used to solve the game. You will be paid based on the time you have entered the correct answers.

**How the game works.** The game runs in real time and is divided into turns of 30 seconds. In each turn you see what has happened since your last turn, and then you decide what to do during the next 30 seconds. In one turn you can:

- **Search** for clues by typing up to 1 search terms. Searches should be single words, so type "Smith" instead of "Mr. Smith". You can search the same keyword more than once to find more clues. Each search returns at most one clue, and you see the results at the start of your next turn. Some clues contain useful information and some don't. Clues are labelled C1, C2, and so on.
- **Send** up to 1 message(s) to the people listed in your messaging window. Writing a message takes time: in a turn in which you send a message with your own text (including a reply), you cannot search. Passing on clues or forwarding a message without adding text is quick and does not stop you from searching.
- **Enter or change your answers.** Your answers stay entered until you change them. Leave an answer empty (null) to keep what you have entered.
- Or do nothing this turn.

**Messaging window.** You follow (see the answers and receive the messages of): Sage. You can send messages to (the people who follow you): Finley, Quinn, Sage.

When you send a message you can write free text, share clues you have (by their labels), or both. You can also reply to a message you received or forward it, by giving its label (M1, M2, and so on). Messages from headquarters are sent to all players.

**Answers.** There are two questions: "Who is the victim?" and "Who is the murderer?". With the murderer you also enter how confident you are in that answer (0 to 100 percent). The people who follow you see your answers and confidence, and you see the answers and confidence of the people you follow. Nobody sees your searches.

**Payment.** The longer you have correct answers entered in the computer, the higher the payment. The base payment is 40 cents. You earn a bonus of 14 cents for each minute you have the correct answer to "Who is the victim?" entered, and 14 cents for each minute you have the correct answer to "Who is the murderer?" entered. You can change your answers at any time. Your confidence shows how sure you are.

The game lasts 15 minutes. It starts now.

**Memory.** Like anyone doing this in real time, you can only keep the last few turns in mind. Older turns, including older search results, messages and notes, are forgotten. Your notes are only for thinking during the current turn. You also have a notepad next to you. In each turn you can scribble up to 15 words on it, the way you would jot something down while working. Everything on your notepad stays in front of you for the rest of the game.
